svg.title: Draw the hump, and the flag
svg.desc: Three empty framed panels. The first is for drawing the fourteen hourly late rates as a shape, with the flat straight line a single weight is forced to draw through them, and the numbers 0.374 at hour 18 and 0.196 at hour 22 marked. The second is for drawing the same information as one yes-or-no column, with the two group rates 0.3682 for rush and 0.2424 for everything else and the subtraction 0.1258 written between them. The third is for drawing one row of an ablation table with the two scores and the subtraction on it. A panel at the bottom says what a good answer contains: a hump and not a slope, the flat line labelled with the fitted weight of minus 0.121 against is_rush's 0.436, the gap of 0.1258 written as a subtraction, and a verdict of keep or delete with a number beside it.
svg.text: Draw the hump, and the flag
The hour matters enormously. The hour as a number does not.
draw the shape, then the best straight line through it
Panel 2 — the same thing as one column
two groups, two rates, one subtraction
Panel 3 — one row of your ablation table
variant, columns, AUC, and the delta to four places
What a good answer looks like
· panel 1 is a hump, not a slope, and the line is nearly flat
· the flat line is labelled −0.121, the flag 0.436
· panel 2 has 0.3682, 0.2424 and the gap 0.1258 on it
· panel 3's delta has four decimal places and a sign
· a verdict word, with the number that justified it
